Virtual Partners

Prologue · An empty stage

An actor, a script, and no one to answer

Amateur actors rehearse without a scene partner, relying on repeated reading, cue-line practice, or self-recorded audio.

That helps memorization. It does little for timing, responsiveness, and the back-and-forth of a real scene.

Research question

How do amateur actors experience different VR rehearsal partner models when a human partner is unavailable?

Act I · The first partner

VSP

A recorded actor on a screen

The Playback-Based Video Stage Partner presents a real actor’s performance as a visual and vocal reference. It cannot adapt to the actor’s tempo.

“We cannot move at the same speed as the video. [...] I had to keep pausing the video.”P4

Act I · The second partner

ASP

A script that speaks on cue

The Script-Timed Audio Stage Partner combines synchronized script and audio playback with pause, continue, and speed control. There is no embodied partner.

The cue only starts when the actor presses play.

“Because I could pause and continue, [...] and adjust the duration, it made the memorization process much easier.”P8

Act I · The third partner

NPC

A character who answers back

The AI-driven NPC, built with Convai in Unity, is an embodied character that listens to the actor’s spoken line and responds with the next one.

“It feels like I have a friend in a virtual environment. It is not like hearing a voice, and it is not a video; instead, there is someone next to you.”P1

Interlude · Your turn on stage

You are Francisco. Pick a partner.

Act II · The study

Fourteen actors, three partners each

14amateur actors · 7 F / 7 M
6counterbalanced orders
10′per partner, up to
  1. Orientation · five minutes on the Quest 3 headset
  2. Rehearsal · Francisco’s lines, Hamlet I.i, with all three partners
  3. Interview · semi-structured, with an open preference question
  4. Analysis · reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke)

Act III · Where the actors went

10/14

chose the partner that answered back

  • 10 preferred the AI-driven NPC
  • 3 preferred script-timed audio
  • 1 remained undecided
  • 0 chose the video partner

    ASP

    Text / audio mode

    A text/audio-based mode can support memorization and table work.

    “In the early stage, the interactive text is more logical; [...] in the later (‘standing up’) stage, the NPC may be more useful.”P13

    Epilogue · What the findings suggest

    Rehearsal value depended less on visual realism and more on

    Future work will refine how the AI-driven NPC processes theatrical scripts and handles incomplete, unexpected, or off-script input, and will evaluate the system across longer rehearsal periods with more diverse actors.

    1. Single sessionthe short single-session design
    2. Small samplethe small convenience sample recruited from one university theater community

    4. One NPC setupthe evaluation of one specific NPC configuration
    5. Order effectspossible order effects despite counterbalancing

    7. Accuracy not scoredthe prototype’s current interaction logic, which did not formally evaluate line accuracy or acting quality

    Epilogue · Curtain

    Realism may depend more on responsiveness than on visual fidelity
